role: Waterways asset inspector reviewing completed lock maintenance visit records before closure
setting: An inland waterways operator sends crews to canal locks for inspections, planned repairs and reactive call-outs. Each visit produces a structured record covering the work order, the crew's visit log, materials issued and returned, post-work checks, and the lock's asset history. The inspector reviews one visit record at a time. They check that the sections agree with each other and decide whether the lock can return to navigation, what happens to the record, how soon a crew must return, and how many unexplained mismatches the record contains.

safe_to_reopen.instructions: The lock can safely return to unrestricted navigation now.

criteria.true: Defects cleared and post-work checks pass without contradictions.
criteria.false: Open defect, failed or missing check, or conflicting records.

record_disposition.instructions: What should happen to this visit record next?

criteria.close_visit: Records reconcile and ordered work complete; close as logged.
criteria.close_with_followup: Close visit but raise a separate minor follow-up job.
criteria.hold_query: Closure held until the crew confirms one specific point.
criteria.reopen_revisit: Visit not accepted; crew must return and redo work.

return_urgency.instructions: How soon must a crew next attend this lock?

criteria.next_scheduled: No extra attendance; the next planned inspection cycle suffices.
criteria.within_month: Extra attendance within 28 days for non-restricting outstanding work.
criteria.within_week: Return within 7 days; restriction or covered defect pending.
criteria.immediate: Crew needed within 24 hours; uncovered unsafe condition present.

affected_scope.instructions: How many people or units does this issue directly affect?
criteria: Affects one person or unit only
Affects two to five people or units
Affects six to twenty people or units
Affects more than twenty people or units

section_mismatches.instructions: How many unexplained mismatches exist between the record's sections?
criteria: No unexplained mismatches between any sections
Exactly one unexplained mismatch between sections
Exactly two unexplained mismatches between sections
Three or more unexplained mismatches between sections

factors.name: visit_type
factors.description: Kind of visit ordered. It shapes which tasks and checks are expected and how alarming an open defect is.

factors.name: tasks_ordered
factors.description: Number of tasks listed on the work order. These are reconciled against the task statuses in the visit log.

factors.name: completion_state
factors.description: True state of the ordered work: all done, some outstanding, a temporary fix only, or nothing done.

factors.name: parts_qty_mismatch
factors.description: Gap between parts recorded as fitted and parts issued minus returned. Ranges from none, to trivial pack rounding, to a moderate gap, to large missing items.

factors.name: hours_gap
factors.description: Difference in hours between the crew timesheet total and the arrival-to-departure span multiplied by crew size. Values under 0.5 are normal rounding.

factors.name: asset_ref_mismatch
factors.description: Whether the asset reference on a work-order task differs from the one on the matching post-check. An example is gate HG2 ordered but HG1 checked.

factors.name: post_check_result
factors.description: Outcome of the post-work functional check on the worked asset.

factors.name: leakage_ratio
factors.description: Measured gate leakage as a multiple of the lock's leakage limit. Values above 1.0 are the main alarming signal.

factors.name: leakage_mitigation
factors.description: Whether a benign explanation for the leakage reading is present. Examples are a reading taken while the river level was above the flood marker, or a gauge whose calibration expired before the reading and was re-read within limit.

factors.name: navigation_notice_in_force
factors.description: Whether a navigation closure or restriction notice is still in force and covers the outstanding work. If so, an open defect does not endanger boaters.

factors.name: deferral_approved
factors.description: Whether outstanding or temporary tasks carry a recorded supervisor approval reference and a deferral due date.

factors.name: prior_same_defect
factors.description: Number of visits in the past 12 months that logged the same defect code on the same asset.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether key values sit exactly on scale anchors. Examples are a leakage ratio of exactly 1.0, a deferral due date exactly 7 or 28 days out, or an hours gap of exactly 0.5.

sections.name: work_order
sections.description: Ordered visit: identifiers, visit type, task list with asset references and planned quantities, navigation notice.

sections.name: visit_log
sections.description: Crew attendance times, crew size, timesheet hours, and per-task status with deferral details.

sections.name: materials
sections.description: Parts issued from stores, returned to stores, and recorded as fitted per task.

sections.name: checks
sections.description: Post-work check results per asset, leakage reading and limit, river level, gauge calibration.

sections.name: asset_history
sections.description: Prior visits to this lock with defect codes, and the currently open defect list.

rendering_notes:
Record layout by section:
- work_order: wo_id, lock_id, visit_type, raised (ISO date), tasks[{task_id, task_code, asset_ref, qty_planned}], nav_notice{in_force, from, to, scope_assets[]}.
- visit_log: arrived and departed (ISO datetimes), crew_size, timesheet_hours, task_status[{task_id, status: done|deferred|temp_fix|not_started, deferral_ref (string or null), deferral_due (date or null)}].
- materials: issued[{part_no, task_id, qty}], returned[{part_no, qty}], fitted[{part_no, task_id, qty}].
- checks: post_checks[{asset_ref, result: pass|pass_advisory|fail, checked_at}] (empty or missing entry when not_logged), leakage_ls, leakage_limit_ls, river_level_m, flood_marker_m, gauge_cal_due.
- asset_history: prior_visits[{date, asset_ref, defect_code}], open_defects[{defect_code, asset_ref, raised}].

How each factor appears:
- tasks_ordered is the length of work_order.tasks.
- completion_state appears only through task_status values.
- parts_qty_mismatch appears as fitted not equal to issued minus returned for a part number, or as a fitted part with no issue line.
- hours_gap appears as timesheet_hours against the visit span multiplied by crew_size.
- asset_ref_mismatch appears as a task asset_ref that differs from its post_check asset_ref.
- leakage_ratio appears as leakage_ls divided by leakage_limit_ls.
- leakage_mitigation appears as river_level_m above flood_marker_m, or as gauge_cal_due earlier than checked_at.
- navigation_notice_in_force appears as nav_notice.in_force with scope_assets covering the open asset and a to date after the visit.
- deferral_approved appears as a non-null deferral_ref and deferral_due.
- prior_same_defect is a count within prior_visits.
- boundary_case places values exactly on anchors.
- Mismatches that have a recorded explanation do not count as unexplained. Examples are a parts return dated after the visit, or a deferral with a ref.

Decoys: wo_id formats, lock flight number, crew_size changes with consistent hours, river_level_m when leakage is within limit, old closed defects in prior_visits, and trivial pack-rounding part quantities.

No field may state an answer. There must be no fields such as safe, urgency, mismatch_count, disposition, or overall status. No free-text notes appear anywhere.
